{{Quote|Whoever has two hands can hold a gaderffii.|Tusken proverb|<ref name="Star Wars (1998) 13">[[Star Wars (1998) 13|''Star Wars'' (1998) 13]]</ref>}}
The '''gaderffii''', or '''gaffi stick''', was the traditional melee weapon of the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. It was a pole weapon with a spike or blade on one end and some kind of bludgeoning instrument on the other.

==Description==
{{Quote|It looks like Sand people did this, all right. Look, there are gaffi sticks, bantha tracks. It's just...I've never heard of them hitting anything this big before.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
Gaderffii sticks were crafted from salvage and scrap [[Metal/Legends|metal]], often scavenged directly from the wrecks of abandoned vehicles and machinery that littered the surface of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Essentially a combination [[Spear/Legends|spear]] and [[Axe/Legends|axe]], gaderffi sticks were used to thrust and slash while attacking, and to parry while defending.<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

Nearly every Tusken was proficient in the use of these weapons, and more Tuskens chose the gaffi over the [[Cycler rifle/Legends|Tusken Cycler]].

[[File:GaderffiiSticks-SWBC8.png|thumb|left|250px|Three different styles of gaffi sticks]]
The weapon was of the staff variety, on average about 120 centimeters long, with a weapon-head on each end. The first resembled an archaic flanged mace, with each of the four or more flanges sharpened like an axe-edge. Upon the tip was a spearpoint. The opposite end of the gaffi stick usually was bent into an L shape, with a large and heavy club head tipped by a hook or second spearpoint (which itself was often tipped with [[Sand bat/Legends|sand bat]] venom) which would inflict maximum pain to an enemy. The dual weapon-heads gave a gaderffii wielder a wide and versatile range of attack options. The axe-mace could chop and hack, the spearpoint could thrust and stab, the club could bludgeon and crush, and the hook could rip and trip an opponent. In a more mundane fashion, the gaffi stick could also be used in many day-to-day survival chores, such as hunting or digging.

[[File:Tusken_Unleashed.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raider]] attacks with a gaderffii.]]
Though the gaderffii were made out of whatever materials the Sand People could find, desired materials included hard metals such as iron and steel. The best gaffi sticks were [[Chieftain's gaderffii]], often seen in hands of veteran warriors or chieftains as a rank symbol. They were made out of the rare [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] plating found on derelict starships or vehicles that had been "slagged" upon Tatooine's surface. Such weapons were highly valued, being exceedingly durable.

Sand People prized their gaderffii, which were largely custom-built and thus identifiable as belonging to particular raiders, and would not part with them willingly. Thus, when bounty hunters were sent to eliminate hostile raiders, they were told to return with their gaffi sticks as proof of the kill.

During [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic#Second Star Map: Tatooine|Revan's search for a Star Map on Tatooine]], the [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] requested that he collect as many gaffi sticks as possible from the Sand People that were attacking Czerka's miners and sandcrawlers.

==Usage==
[[File:Gaffi_stick_TCG_by_Hustak.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Tusken Raider wielding his gaffi stick]]
This weapon was the traditional weapon of the Tusken Raiders of Tatooine.

Many [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] adopted this weapon as a useful multipurpose tool and melee weapon.<ref name="TRG1-52" />

[[Ewok Handler]]s also carried these lethal weapons.

==Behind the scenes==
According to oceanic art expert Bruno Claessens, the original gaffi sticks props were inspired by wooden [[Wikipedia:Fiji|Fijian]] war clubs called [[Wikipedia:Totokia|totokia]].<ref name="Bruno Claessens">{{WebCite|url=http://brunoclaessens.com/2015/07/george-lucas-star-wars-and-oceanic-art|text=George Lucas' "Star Wars" and Oceanic art|work=[https://brunoclaessens.com Bruno Claessens]|archivedate=20201205114353}}</ref>
